speedrun.lead: The whole game with Hazel’s rules takes about 3% longer than in plain JavaScript, now that Hazel decides much more of it, as it did before the animals moved: Gnome world’s speed run took 27.2 s against 26.4 s on 11-27 (588 against 570 µs a step), and 25.5 s against 24.7 s on 11-25.
speedrun.body: The rules’ own share grew with what they decide, from 0.34 s of the run (1.3%) on 11-25 to 0.90 s (3.3%) now, the birds alone 261,889 calls and 0.36 s of it; in plain JavaScript the same calls took 0.60 s. The rest of each step is the page’s JavaScript, as it was: the water, the rest of the world, the speed run’s own way-finding. The third way, the interpreter, did not start on 0.0.148: its page had no rules when the run restarted it, which is to be looked into; on 11-25 it took 227.6 s for 42,000 steps, 88.6% of them in the rules (^report(65)).
speedrun.cap: Gnome world’s speed run, the whole game from a fresh world to its end, in headless Chrome on GitHub’s machines (node/world-speedrun.mjs): 11-25 at bbfde10 (^report(65), its rules compiled in the page by the hazeljs branch’s library) and 11-27 at 0.0.148, 5e43910 (run 46025660460, its rules compiled ahead of time with the night’s trials, made in 188 ms). The worlds of the two days differ (the run took 44,933 steps then, about 46,270 now), so compare within a day. Plain JavaScript is ⚡: the page’s own JavaScript for each piece.
